<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With tensor parallelism every row-parallel layer (`o_proj`, `down_proj`, linear-attention `out_proj`) rounds its per-rank partial sum to BF16 before the all-reduce, while a single GPU rounds the full sum once. The extra rounding is small on average but explodes where the two halves cancel, which is frequent: on real Qwen3-4B / Qwen3-14B activations at TP=2, outputs whose error exceeds 1% of the row's RMS occur **4.75x / 5.53x as often as on one GPU**. Converting the BF16 partials to FP32 before the all-reduce (#50972) cannot help at TP=2: the rounding has already happened, and the result is bit-identical.

This PR adds `VLLM_TP_FP16_PARTIAL_SUMS=1` (off by default): the row-parallel GEMM writes its partial sum in FP16 (8x finer than BF16, same bytes on the wire), the all-reduce runs in FP16, and the output is rounded to BF16 once, after the sum, as on one GPU; an exact power-of-two prescale (2^-2 by default) keeps partial sums far from the FP16 range limit. The large-error events return to the single-GPU level, the BF16 output gets measurably closer to an FP32 reference than both TP=2 today and TP=1, and throughput does not change.

**Not a duplicate of #50972.** That PR upcasts the BF16 partial sums to FP32 before the all-reduce; at TP=2 this is bit-identical to today (`bf16(a) + bf16(b)` is exact in FP32), because the extra rounding happens earlier, when each rank's GEMM writes BF16. This PR changes the precision of the partial sums themselves. Related: #40725 (did not reproduce on our setup, see Details), #57042.

## Claims

- Opt-in FP16 partial sums for tensor-parallel row-parallel layers: unquantized BF16 layers, NVFP4 CUTLASS and block-scaled FP8 CUTLASS/Triton kernels. Default behavior unchanged.
- At the source (real activations, TP=2 emulated per layer): errors > 1% of the row RMS per token, Qwen3-4B 712 -> 155 (one GPU: 150), Qwen3-14B 1,441 -> 271 (one GPU: 260).
- At the output, Qwen3-4B BF16, 292k tokens: NLL excess over an FP32 reference +0.00062 -> **+0.00039** (TP=1: +0.00058); agreement with TP=1 at near-tied tokens improves (p 0.012-0.049).
- No throughput change (Qwen3-4B TP=2 decode: batch 1 -0.9%, batch 16 +-0%); bytes exchanged unchanged; GSM8K unchanged (`tests/evals`, see Validation).
- Quantized models (FP8, W4A4): same source-level reduction; output-level differences at the edge of significance or within activation-quantization noise in our measurements.

## Validation

2x RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB (SM120, PCIe 5.0 x8 each, no P2P), torch 2.14 / CUDA 13.0, vLLM main + this PR. Text: Wikipedia history articles in en/it/es/fr (CC BY-SA), 1,500-token chunks (292,500 tokens) and 4 x 16k-token chunks. The output-level numbers below were produced by this PR's code; later commits only restructure the block-FP8 kernel call and move the tests (FP8 results re-checked: KL 2.6e-6 to the measured run). Scripts, patch and result summaries: [capy-flash/bench/vllm_tp_partial_sums](https://github.com/ValerioDolci/capy-flash/tree/main/bench/vllm_tp_partial_sums) (`run_all.sh <models dir> <out dir>`).

**Tests and checks** (on this branch):

| command | result |
|---|---|
| `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` | all hooks pass (ruff, mypy, typos, SPDX, CI wiring, ...) |
| `pytest tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py -k fp16_partial_sums` | 2 passed: `test_tp_fp16_partial_sums_scale_is_exact_and_saturates` (1 GPU: the 2^-k prescale is exact, out-of-range partials saturate instead of inf) and `test_tp_fp16_partial_sums_row_parallel` (2 GPUs: a real TP=2 `RowParallelLinear`; with the flag the error against a float64 reference stays < 1.05x the single-GPU error, without it it is > 1.2x) |
| `pytest tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py -k test_multi_process_tensor_parallel` | existing TP=2 tests: 3 passed |
| `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error VLLM_TP_FP16_PARTIAL_SUMS=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B -tp 2` + GSM8K | no host synchronization reported |
| `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --use-chat-completions --max-tokens 1024 --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' --temperature 0` against `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B -tp 2`, 3 runs per arm | flag off 0.859 / 0.853 / 0.859, flag on 0.855 / 0.857 / 0.856 (1,319 questions; run-to-run batching noise of the same size) |

**1. Error at the source.** Model in BF16 on one GPU (HF transformers); in every row-parallel call the two TP=2 halves are computed in FP32 and combined as one GPU `bf16(a+b)`, TP=2 today `bf16(bf16(a)+bf16(b))`, this PR `bf16(4 * (fp16(a/4)+fp16(b/4)))`. Error = |output - (a+b)| / RMS(row); counts per token, 95% bootstrap CI over 32 chunks.

| errors per token | one GPU | TP=2 BF16 | TP=2 FP16 (PR) | BF16 / one GPU |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-4B, > 1% of row RMS | 150 [149, 151] | 712 [709, 715] | 155 [154, 156] | 4.75 [4.72, 4.78] |
| Qwen3-4B, > 0.1% | 68,033 | 95,036 | 68,748 | 1.40 |
| Qwen3-14B, > 1% | 260 [258, 263] | 1,441 [1,433, 1,447] | 271 [268, 273] | 5.53 [5.50, 5.57] |
| Qwen3-14B, > 0.1% | 150,999 | 210,982 | 152,653 | 1.40 |

Same excess in all four languages, in both projections (4B: `o_proj` 381 vs 88, `down_proj` 332 vs 62) and over all layers.

**2. Output, Qwen3-4B BF16, teacher-forced top-20 log-probabilities, 292,500 tokens.** References: the same model on one GPU (TP=1) and in FP32 (TP=2). Forks = positions where the TP=1 top-2 log-probabilities are within a margin; paired McNemar on top-1 agreement.

| | TP=1 | TP=2 BF16 | TP=2 FP16 (PR) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| NLL excess over FP32 (95% CI) | +0.00058 [0.00044, 0.00071] | +0.00062 [0.00049, 0.00076] | **+0.00039** [0.00025, 0.00051] |
| KL to FP32 | 6.76e-4 | 6.69e-4 | **6.45e-4** |
| NLL vs TP=1, paired | | +0.00005 [-0.00013, 0.00022] | -0.00019 [-0.00036, -0.00002] |
| top-1 = TP=1 at forks < 0.25 (25,804) | | 86.1% | 86.6% (p 0.015) |
| top-1 = TP=1 at forks < 0.5 (52,975) | | 93.0% | 93.3% (p 0.012) |
| positions with KL to TP=1 > 0.1 | | 43 | 28 (p 0.018) |

**3. Quantized models** (TP=1 reference; via UVA offload for the 27B).

| model | metric | TP=2 BF16 | TP=2 FP16 (PR) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-8B-FP8 (block FP8, `--linear-backend cutlass`), 292k tokens | KL to TP=1 | 6.42e-3 | 6.38e-3 |
| | positions with KL > 0.1 | 1,778 | 1,678 (p 0.035) |
| | top-1 = TP=1 at forks < 0.25 | 71.1% | 70.6% (p 0.11) |
| Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 (W4A4, 64 layers), 24k tokens | perplexity (TP=1 5.7509) | 5.7559 | 5.7617 (difference CI spans 0) |

**4. Throughput** (Qwen3-4B BF16, TP=2, 256 generated tokens): batch 1 126.0 -> 124.9 tok/s, batch 16 1,653 -> 1,652 tok/s.

<details>
<summary>More: cancellation ratio, long context, MoE, #40725, earlier builds</summary>

- Cancellation ratio `r = (|a|+|b|)/|a+b|` on real activations (same on 4B and 14B): r > 64 for 0.89% of the exchanged elements, r > 512 for 0.11%, p99.99 = 5,856 (4B). Qwen3-4B exchanges 184,320 elements per token at TP=2, Qwen3-14B 409,600.
- Largest |partial sum| seen: 7,986 (4B), 14,664 (14B, `down_proj`): only 4.5x below the FP16 limit, hence the default 2^-2 prescale (18x margin); error counts are identical with k = 0 and k = 2.
- 16k-token contexts (earlier build of the same change, k = 0): the FP16 arm is closer to FP32 than the BF16 arm at every depth beyond 1k tokens (8k-16k: KL 6.87e-4 vs 7.40e-4, TP=1 6.86e-4); the distance does not grow with depth.
- MoE: on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 (experts W4A16) TP=2 and expert parallelism are at the same distance from TP=1 (KL 8.2e-3 vs 8.3e-3), so the MoE reduction is not targeted here.
- #40725: not reproduced with vLLM main on this setup (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4, the issue's prompts in es/it/pt/en, sampled and greedy, TP=2 / expert parallel / FP16 model: 0 broken words in 24 poems).
- GSM8K (1,319, greedy) on Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4, earlier build: 0.9393 vs 0.9393; with bit-identical numerics vLLM batching alone flips 34 answers between runs, so GSM8K cannot resolve effects of this size.

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** A row-parallel layer at TP=2 computes `a = x[:, :K/2] W[:, :K/2]^T` and `b = x[:, K/2:] W[:, K/2:]^T` with FP32 accumulation, writes them as BF16, and all-reduces. Rounding `a` and `b` separately adds an error proportional to `|a| + |b|`, not to `|a + b|`; where the halves cancel, it dominates. `bf16(a) + bf16(b)` is exact in FP32, so upcasting the BF16 partials before the all-reduce leaves the result bit-identical at TP=2 (checked on 2^20 random pairs).

**Change.** `RowParallelLinear` decides once at construction (`_fp16_partials_mode`) whether FP16 partials apply: TP > 1, `reduce_results`, BF16 params, CUDA, not batch-invariant, and either the default unquantized GEMM (computed here with `torch.mm(..., out_dtype=float32)` then scaled, saturated and cast to FP16, since there is no BF16 -> FP16 GEMM output) or a quantized kernel declaring `supports_partial_sum_dtype` (NVFP4 CUTLASS; block FP8 CUTLASS/Triton). Those kernels read `layer.partial_sum_dtype` / `partial_sum_scale`, write FP16 directly and fold the scale into parameters they already take (NVFP4 `alpha`, FP8 weight block scales). After the all-reduce the output is cast to BF16 and multiplied by 2^k. No host synchronization is added in forward (all decisions are Python values fixed at construction); the default path is unchanged.

**Tradeoffs / limits.** On Hopper (SM90) and SM100, where the all-reduce + RMSNorm fusion pass is enabled by default, the FP16 all-reduce no longer matches the fused pattern, so enabling the flag there trades that fusion for accuracy; we could not measure it (no such hardware). FP16 range: values that still exceed 65504 * 2^k saturate instead of becoming inf. Partials below 2^-14 * 2^k lose relative precision to FP16 subnormals (absolute error <= 2^-24 * 2^k, far below the BF16 rounding of normal rows). Not covered: other FP8/NVFP4 kernels (DeepGEMM, the default block-FP8 kernel on SM120, Marlin, FlashInfer), the MoE expert reduction, sequence-parallel reduce-scatter. Measured at TP=2 only (two GPUs); at TP=N each rank rounds 1/N of the sum, so the excess is expected to grow with N. The 2-GPU test runs where the existing `test_comm_ops.py` TP=2 tests run; the model-level validation above ran outside CI. Possible follow-ups we left to the maintainers' judgement: precomputing the scaled `alpha` / weight scales instead of scaling per call, and a single output-dtype signature for all block-FP8 kernels (today only the two covered kernels implement `apply_block_scaled_mm_out`).

**Origin.** We found this while investigating why TP=2 runs of [capy-flash](https://github.com/ValerioDolci/capy-flash) (Apache-2.0, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 with tensor parallelism over PCIe on two consumer GPUs) drifted from a single-GPU reference; there, FP16/FP32 partial sums removed ~85% of the TP=2-vs-single-GPU distance to the reference logits. All numbers above are measured on vLLM.

**AI assistance.** This change, its measurements and this description were prepared with AI assistance (Claude); I reviewed the diff and the results and ran the tests listed above.

The 2-GPU test runs where the existing `test_comm_ops.py` TP=2 tests run; the model-level validation above ran outside CI. Possible follow-ups we left to the maintainers' judgement: precomputing the scaled `alpha` / weight scales instead of scaling per call, and a single output-dtype signature for all block-FP8 kernels (today only the two covered kernels implement `apply_block_scaled_mm_out`).

**Origin.** We found this while investigating why TP=2 runs of [capy-flash](https://github.com/ValerioDolci/capy-flash) (Apache-2.0, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 with tensor parallelism over PCIe on two consumer GPUs) drifted from a single-GPU reference; there, FP16/FP32 partial sums removed ~85% of the TP=2-vs-single-GPU distance to the reference logits. All numbers above are measured on vLLM.

**AI assistance.** This change, its measurements and this description were prepared with AI assistance (Claude); I reviewed the diff and the results and ran the tests listed above.

+@ray.remote(num_gpus=1, max_calls=1)
+def fp16_partial_sums_row_parallel_test_worker(
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
+    tp_size: int,
+    pp_size: int,
+    rank: int,
+    distributed_init_port: str,
+):
+    """VLLM_TP_FP16_PARTIAL_SUMS: a TP row-parallel layer with FP16 partial sums
+    keeps the single-GPU error against an exact reference; BF16 partials do not."""
+    from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.linear import RowParallelLinear
+
+    monkeypatch.delenv("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES", raising=False)
+    device = torch.device(f"cuda:{rank}")
+    torch.accelerator.set_device_index(device)
+    init_test_distributed_environment(tp_size, pp_size, rank, distributed_init_port)
+
+    m, k, n = 64, 4096, 2048
+    shard = slice(rank * k // tp_size, (rank + 1) * k // tp_size)
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0)
+    x = torch.randn(m, k, device="cuda", generator=gen).bfloat16()
+    w = (torch.randn(n, k, device="cuda", generator=gen) / k**0.5).bfloat16()
+    exact = x.double() @ w.double().T
+    rms = exact.pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True).sqrt()
+
+    def error(out: torch.Tensor) -> float:
+        return float(((out.double() - exact).abs() / rms).mean())
+
+    errors = {}
+    for flag in ("0", "1"):
+        monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_TP_FP16_PARTIAL_SUMS", flag)
+        with set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()), torch.device("cuda"):
+            layer = RowParallelLinear(k, n, bias=False, params_dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        assert layer._fp16_partials == ("gemm" if flag == "1" else None)
+        layer.weight.data.copy_(w[:, shard])
+        out, _ = layer(x[:, shard])
+        assert out.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        errors[flag] = error(out)
+    one_gpu = error(exact.bfloat16())
+    assert errors["1"] < 1.05 * one_gpu, (errors, one_gpu)
+    assert errors["0"] > 1.2 * one_gpu, (errors, one_gpu)
+

+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.linear import _fp16_partial_linear

+    normal = plain.float().abs() >= 2.0**-14 * 4

+    c = (1.5 * fp16_max / float((x.double() @ w.double().T).abs().max())) ** 0.5
+    xb, wb = (x.float() * c).bfloat16(), (w.float() * c).bfloat16()
+    ref = xb.double() @ wb.double().T
+    assert ref.abs().max() > fp16_max
+    saturated = _fp16_partial_linear(xb, wb, None, 1.0)
+    assert torch.isfinite(saturated).all()
+    in_range = _fp16_partial_linear(xb, wb, None, 0.25).double() * 4
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
